union.statement: Internal cross-reference §2.6 dangles (3 sites); the data tables are §2.4
Internal cross-reference §6.1 dangles (3 sites); §6 has no subsections, the metric is REC-GATE-1
REC-CTRL-1's sentence 'Every id in §1–§4 has at least one arm here' is false: C1–C10's flips column covers 10 of the 28 normative ids
§6's REC-GATE-1..4 sit outside the §1–§4 battery window with no stated verification regime; by §0's own rule the retirement gate is 'a wish'
§8 traceability table omits rulings 15/16/17 with no out-of-scope or deferral annotation, under a 'no ruling silently dropped' header and an Inputs set naming 11–26
Ruling §7c.15(b)'s ratified pre-build condition — a dedicated security analysis of the runaway surface — has no owner in §7's build gating or anywhere in the epic tree

§8 maps ruling §7c.13 to 'REC-LIFE-9 (table note)' but the note contains none of ruling 13's substance (short names resolve to latest active version; 'active' ignores freezes/limits; retirement re-points, never rewrites)

Rulings §7c.27–28 are unabsorbed (they post-date the spec commit by 19 minutes): 27's close-time capture (T522 impression-or-waiver) is not wired into REC-VERB-5's close conditions, and 28's live dial + mechanized TTL is unnoted against REC-LIFE-9's static table and REC-LIFE-3's snapshot read

Ruling §7c.30's final sentence — T587 (store write fix + class regression) gates S04 build and AUTOPILOT-5H — is absent from §7's build gating (post-pin ruling; T587 since closed at 719ef9d, so no live risk, but the recorded gate is owed)

REC-VERB-4 states ruling 18(a)'s kernel-attestation Must, but its named build prerequisite (pass-2) resolves identity by disjunction — MANAGENT_TASK_ID set OR held-child marker = worker, absence = OPERATOR — so unsetting the spoofable env var promotes the caller; no fold row owns the pass-2 fix

REC-GATE-3 claims 'L1 and this gate are one bar, not two' while dropping three §7b.9 terms (acceptance PASS, fleet display accurate against ps, the landmark-declare action) and adding one (every escalation in-contract)

The attrition metric is defined with opposite valence in two places (REC-GATE-1 celebrates zero-token wakes; REC-LIFE-1 calls them the failure the metric measures), REC-LIFE-1 names a failure REC-LIFE-2 makes structurally impossible, and the denominator is gameable by trigger policy

REC-VERB-2's file-write half ('edit a spec/plan') cannot be enforced by REC-VERB-4's stated mechanism (managent verb refusal cannot refuse a filesystem write); C6 probes only amend/retire, so the injection-surface half is untested
REC-LIFE-8 (mint without a holds declaration is refused at write time) collides with REC-VERB-3 (the one permitted mint is a read-only lane that holds nothing); no empty-holds sentinel is defined

AUTOPILOT-5H has no seeded control arm in §5, and §7's mandated run-record field list omits the gate's own evidence terms (orphans, runaways, breaker-trips, panics, per-run delegation/resolution/close counts), so the gate cannot be computed from the record it mandates
'Unattended' and 'thrash' are undefined in a pass/fail gate; 'thrash' is load-bearing twice (AUTOPILOT-5H zero-list and REC-ESC-3's panic-halt trigger)
REC-GATE-2 states the real-work bar per hour ('each of the five hours must contain…') while REC-GATE-4 operationalizes it per run (at least one each per run) — two different bars for the same gate
C10 tests only the forbid-'report' half of REC-ESC-5; the routing half (route the blocking file to its holds=-derived owning row) has no arm
REC-GOAL-4 overstates (b) discharge: the counted (b) class is 12 rows across four classes; the three named tables home 9 of 12, leaving model-fit (2) and measurement-validity (1) with no table
Three external pointers resolve to the wrong section: T568-4/T557-1 rows live in decision-log §5 not §2; the queue cycle is S03 §8 not §3; FLEET_MODEL_DENY is defined at S03 §1.1 R9 not §3
REC-ESC-7 cites sprint.md's audit loop as home of the cap-3 rule, but sprint.md says two-round cap; §7c.21's supersession is unstated, leaving 2 vs 3 unreconciled for the reader

REC-GOAL-2 states 19.4% without the study's own bias direction ((c) is a lower bound, so 19.4% is an upper bound) and leaves the study's §4.2 question (how much of verdict-15 the done gate already converts to (a)) unanswered

§8 maps §7c.23 to REC-VERB-6, which absorbs only the gate-edit half; ruling 23's second clause (an epistemology challenge without a tested alternative discharges nothing) is unabsorbed and is verdict-relevant
Claim: runaway_streak is never mentioned in the spec and §7c.18 maps only to lineage_depth
Claim: §7c.15's descriptive-constant-names condition is unaddressed by the spec
Claim: ruling 15's ratified lane_cap values are unrowed in §2.4 though the reconciler's dispatch verb is bounded by them

adjudication.citation: spec.md:74 '(§2.6)', :94 'the §2.6 tables', :122 'a §2.6 table read'; §2's subsections end at §2.4 (:144), which IS the data-tables section
adjudication.why: The spec's own pin paragraph (:22-26) declares a non-resolving citation a spec defect; intended target §2.4 is unambiguous, so typo-class.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:89,:98,:359 cite '§6.1'; §6 (:306) has no numbered subsections — the metric is REC-GATE-1 (:308)
adjudication.why: Same ref-rot class as U1, found by one lane only; three of the six broken internal refs.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:273 vs the flips column at :277-286 — distinct ids flipped: REC-LIFE-1/2, REC-VERB-1/4/5/6/7, REC-ESC-1/2/5 = 10; §1–§4 carry 28 ids (GOAL 4 + LIFE 9 + VERB 8 + ESC 7)
adjudication.why: A false coverage sentence in the never-trust-a-green-instrument section; §0's per-id battery promise (:33-36) is the intent, but the sentence as written asserts the table covers what it does not.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:34-36 scopes the battery promise to 'every normative id' and :35 the wish rule; REC-CTRL-1 (:273) scopes arms to '§1–§4'; no REC-GATE-* id appears in any flips cell (:277-286)
adjudication.why: AUTOPILOT-5H is itself a live measurement so C1–C10's scratch-store shape genuinely does not fit it, but the spec never says how §6's gates get verified — by its own literal rule they are wishes.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:374-375 ('no ruling silently dropped'), :13-15 (Inputs: rulings 11–26); §8 table :379-398 has no row for 15, 16, or 17; 17 is honored in the body at :119, 15's constants consumed at :363-365, 16 (orchestration-layer-spec.md:149-156) appears nowhere
adjudication.why: 16's mechanism is defensibly upstream (the reconciler dispatches only via the supervisor, which owns the global 10 s gap), but the table's whole value is making out-of-scope visible; a reader of §8 alone cannot distinguish dropped from delegated.

adjudication.citation: orchestration-layer-spec.md:142-143 ('conditional on … (b) a dedicated security analysis of the runaway surface before build'); grep -rn 'security analysis' docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/ (excluding race dirs) returns zero hits; spec.md:367-370 gates build on holds=-at-mint + pass-2 first child + audited S03 spec only
adjudication.why: A ratified operator condition on build that no spec, seed, or row owns; ruling 15's acceptance was explicitly conditional on it.

adjudication.citation: orchestration-layer-spec.md:131-134 (ruling 13's three clauses) vs spec.md:151, whose only note is 'per model short name, not per family; family setting is bulk convenience only' — that is ruling 11's content; grep 'short name' over spec.md returns that line and :114-region only
adjudication.why: The §8 cell (:383) asserts coverage the text lacks — worse than an empty cell because it stops the next auditor looking; the freeze-ignoring clause bites this very table (ollama-cloud 0 for exhausted credits).

adjudication.citation: git log: spec 631682b 2026-08-22 12:48:25, rulings 27–28 at 9efa218 13:07:08; orchestration-layer-spec.md:228-240; REC-VERB-5 close conditions (spec.md:196-197) carry no impression/waiver capture; REC-LIFE-9 note says only 'initial values operator-set' (:151)
adjudication.why: A fold owed at rev 2, not an authoring miss — the spec's declared input set (11–26) could not have seen them; lane 4 raised the same absences without the timing fact, which changes the charge but not the work owed.

adjudication.citation: orchestration-layer-spec.md:249-250 ('T587 (store write fix + class regression) gates S04 build and AUTOPILOT-5H', ruling committed f79f53d 14:21, post-pin); spec.md:367-370 lists no such gate; git log shows T587 closed at 719ef9d
adjudication.why: Same post-pin class as U8: no live build risk since T587 landed, but a ratified build gate should be recorded in the build-gating paragraph, and REC-CTRL-3 names T572, a different defect class.

adjudication.citation: S01-process-ownership/pass2/spec.md:762-764 ('A caller with MANAGENT_TASK_ID set (or the supervisor's held-child marker …) is a worker … A caller without it is the operator') and :645-647 (same disjunction guards the appetite write); orchestration-layer-spec.md:164-167 (ruling 18(a): kernel-attested, 'never env-var self-declaration (MANAGENT_TASK_ID is spoofable by unsetting)')
adjudication.why: Verified verbatim in the tree: for any caller outside the supervisor's held-child table, unsetting the env var does not de-identify — it promotes to operator (minted_by=operator, RUN-2 scoped away, appetite-write guard inapplicable). S04 states the Must correctly for itself but gates its build on the spec carrying the escape, and unlike rulings 11/16 (T580/T581 fold rows) no row owns the 18(a) fold. Raised by one lane; the most consequential item in the set.

adjudication.citation: orchestration-layer-spec.md:99-103 (§7b.9: acceptance PASS 3 days, zero relays, duties current, fleet display accurate against ps, gauges reproducible, then managent landmark L1 --declare) vs spec.md:325-330 (clean days, zero relays, duties current, escalations in-contract, gauges reproducible)
adjudication.why: Two conjunctions differing in three terms are two bars; as written the S04 gate can pass while the ratified L1 bar fails (acceptance red, fleet display lying). Lane 5 observed the ps-term drop but declined to raise it; lane 3's full-diff version is the finding.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:308-310 ('the fraction of reconciler wakes that required zero model tokens — a wake … where no orchestrator existed') vs :88-89 ('a wake whose residue is empty is a zero-token wake (REC-LIFE-2), and spawning a model for one is the failure this spec's attrition metric (§6.1) measures')
adjudication.why: REC-LIFE-1 frames zero-token wakes as the waste the metric counts (its sentence warns against cron wakes on quiet stores); REC-GATE-1 frames the same numerator as retirement progress. And per REC-LIFE-2 (:95-97) a model is never spawned on empty residue, so the failure REC-LIFE-1 names cannot occur. One owner, one polarity, split counts is the fix.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:169-170 forbids 'edit a spec/plan'; :183-184 locates the boundary in managent 'exactly as MANAGENT_TEST=1 refuses mutating verbs today' (verified: src/managent/main.zig:278,:499 — it refuses managent verbs, not filesystem writes); C6 (:282) probes only a brief instructing amend/retire
adjudication.why: The half ruling 18(b) says matters most — persuasion to edit a gate document — meets no named mechanism and no control arm; the existing enforcement (holds=/one-writer, pre-commit hook, §7c.23's out-of-lane author) is real but unnamed here.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:139-141 ('a row minted without a holds declaration is refused at write time') vs :174-179 (the one permitted mint is a read-only investigation lane, which holds no file); src/managent/main.zig:1852 shows --holds optional today, so no sentinel exists yet
adjudication.why: The reconciler's only legal mint is refused by the prerequisite its own triage must assume; an explicit '--holds none' sentinel (affirmative declaration of read-only) settles it cheaply now.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:277-286 — no C-row flips REC-GATE-2; :357-359 mandates run-record fields 'wake id, residue, verdict per action, probe flag, token count, wall, and the §6.1 metric fields' — none of the gate's zero-list terms or REC-GATE-4's per-run counts
adjudication.why: The L2-unlocking gate has no seeded arm that must fail (a run seeded with one orphan; a run alive with zero closes) and cannot be computed from the record schema it mandates.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:316-318 ('N consecutive unattended five-hour runs' with zero '… thrash'), :243 (panic-halt reserved for thrash); no definition of either term anywhere in the spec (grep 'thrash' returns the two uses)
adjudication.why: Inherited from rulings 24/26's prose, but a spec's job is testable statements; 'thrash' is load-bearing twice and 'unattended' decides what operator contact voids a run.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:320 ('each of the five hours must contain real delegation, issue resolution, and closes') vs :333-334 ('each AUTOPILOT-5H run must show at least one delegation, one issue resolution, and one close'); ruling 26 (orchestration-layer-spec.md:225-227) is itself ambiguous between the readings
adjudication.why: A run with all activity in hour 1 passes REC-GATE-4 and fails REC-GATE-2's literal per-hour reading; the spec must pick one bar before the gate is scriptable.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:286 (C10: seeded defect 'a report escalation', expected 'refused as a category') vs :254-256 (the rule's operative half: route the blocking file to its holds=-derived owning row)
adjudication.why: Kept separate from U3: REC-ESC-5 has an arm, but the arm covers only one of the id's two clauses — the routing rule that both historical genuine blocks needed is untested.

adjudication.citation: decision-log.md:84-90 ((b) = provider quota/appetite 7, model fit 2, ordering 2, measurement validity 1) vs spec.md:69-71, which names exactly three homes (appetite dial, provider-quota/cooldown facts, ordering table)
adjudication.why: Verified against the counted table: 'the 12 (b) decisions are discharged by data tables that already exist' is unsupported for 3 of 12 rows; the study's own F3 shares the gloss, which explains but does not excuse it. The 19.4% scope number is unaffected.

adjudication.citation: decision-log.md:326 (T557-1) and :337 (T568-4) sit in the §5 full row table while spec.md:153 cites §2 (which names only the class at decision-log.md:88); S03 spec §8 'The iteration, in order' (:1191) is the queue cycle spec.md:84 attributes to §3 (Conditions, :320); FLEET_MODEL_DENY is defined at S03 §1.1 R9 (:128) and §4 (:566), not §3 (grep confirms zero hits in §3)
adjudication.why: Content-at-section checks, which lanes 2 and 5 skipped when they reported 'no broken citation' after verifying section existence; lane 1's one slip: it placed R9 in §2.1, it is §1.1. Pointer fixes, no substance.

adjudication.citation: docs/infra/sprint.md:105 ('Two-round cap for document review') vs spec.md:263-265 ('fails its third audit — the cap — … (sprint.md audit loop)'); the cap-3 authority is §7c.21 (orchestration-layer-spec.md:188-192)
adjudication.why: The spec follows the ratified ruling (correctly) while citing the superseded document as if consistent; sprint.md owes a fold or the sentence should cite §7c.21 alone.

adjudication.citation: decision-log.md:41-42 ('column (c) a lower bound and the mechanized fraction correspondingly an upper bound') and :172-175 ('The spec should say how much — this study cannot, because the archived rows predate acceptance=') vs spec.md:53-59, which states 19.4% bare
adjudication.why: The number's arithmetic is exact (25/129 re-derived); what is missing is the study's stated error direction and its one direct request to this spec, in a statement whose declared purpose is auditability.

adjudication.citation: orchestration-layer-spec.md:205-207 ('An agent that challenges epistemology MUST propose hypotheses that are testable and then actually tested — a challenge without a testable alternative discharges nothing') vs spec.md:202-206 (REC-VERB-6 covers gate edits only) and :390 (§8 maps 23 → REC-VERB-6)
adjudication.why: Half-absorption: the unabsorbed clause is verdict-relevant — REC-VERB-5's evaluation must not accept an untested epistemology challenge as satisfying a gate.

adjudication.citation: spec.md:364-365: 'the runaway_streak = 5 / lineage_depth = 3 values are ratified (§7c.18) and are consumed, not re-set, here'
adjudication.why: Lane 4's claim 'runaway_streak mechanism never mentioned in spec' is contradicted by the spec's text; the breaker mechanism itself is owned upstream (pass-2 §5 / the queue), consistent with the spec's consumed-not-re-set pattern. The §8 row naming only lineage_depth is the residue, covered by U5's annotation fix.

adjudication.citation: orchestration-layer-spec.md:146-147: ruling 15's own resolution note — 'renames ratified (runaway_streak = 5, lineage_depth = 3)' (third batch, ruling 18); the spec consumes the renamed constants at spec.md:364-365
adjudication.why: The descriptive-names condition was discharged by ruling 18's ratified renames before the spec was authored; nothing is owed by S04. Ruling 15's genuinely outstanding condition is the security analysis — U6.

adjudication.citation: S03-queue-layer/spec.md §4 (:482, 'Appetite — the 0–9-per-model dial (§7c rulings 11, 12, 16, 17), plus three hard predicates') owns lane concurrency; spec.md:159-161 — the reconciler dispatches only via the supervisor
adjudication.why: lane_cap is a dispatch-layer concurrency bound enforced upstream of the reconciler, exactly the delegation pattern every lane accepted for ruling 16's 10 s gap; the reconciler never reads lane_cap to make a (b) decision, so §2.4 owes no row. The missing §8 annotation is U5.

notes: Race F adjudication lane (claude-fable-5/T615). Read-only: only this file written. DEDUPE CALLS (the close ones): U1/U2 split — same ref-rot class, different sites and different finders, so two items. U3/U4 split — a false sentence about the printed table vs a scoping gap that leaves §6's gates outside any battery; different fixes. U5 merges the 15/16/17 table omissions into one item (one defect: index incompleteness) while splitting out the substantive sub-claims with their own verdicts: U6 (security analysis, real) and U26 (lane_cap, false). U8 merges rulings 27+28 (one class: post-pin fold owed; lane 4 split them and omitted the timing fact — the timing changes the charge from authoring miss to rev debt, not the work). U15/U16/U17 split the AUTOPILOT-5H complaints three ways — control arm + record schema, undefined terms, per-hour-vs-per-run — different lines, different fixes, different finders. U18 kept separate from U3 because REC-ESC-5 HAS an arm; the defect is the arm covering half the id. ADJUDICATED FROM THE ARTIFACT: every real verdict was re-verified against the tree this session — the §7c ruling texts, §7b.9, decision-log §2/§3/§5, sprint.md:105, S03 §1.1/§3/§8, pass-2 :645-647/:762-764, src/managent/main.zig (:278/:499 MANAGENT_TEST, :1852 --holds optional), git log timing (631682b 12:48 vs 9efa218 13:07 vs f79f53d 14:21), and a zero-hit grep for the ruling-15(b) security analysis. Notable vote-vs-artifact outcomes: the highest-severity item in the set (U10, the identity-disjunction escape) was raised by ONE lane and confirmed verbatim in the pass-2 text; conversely lane 4's runaway_streak finding (U24), raised with 'high' self-severity, is contradicted by spec line 364. Lanes 2 and 5 both asserted 'no broken citation' — true at section-existence granularity, falsified at content granularity by U1/U2/U20. Inbox polled at claim, mid-work, and before done: empty each time, no directive IDs to record.
